PreToolUse._comment: The matcher names the GitHub MCP tools and the desktop app's own mcp__ccd_pr__set_auto_merge alongside Bash because guard_ship.py guards them too (web-auditor#224: PR #185 was merged through mcp__github__merge_pull_request while this hook was registered against Bash alone, and it never fired; A18 found set_auto_merge unguarded the same way, by grep rather than by an incident). The matcher and the tool sets in guard_ship.py are pinned to each other by its self-test -- change them together. The trailing `|| { ... }` is the outermost failure layer: it fires when python cannot start at all, which the hook's own try/except cannot reach. A20 gave that layer the same two properties the crash layer already had. It is FILTERED -- the `case` arms are guard_ship.py's CRASH_RECHECK_WORDS, also pinned by the self-test -- because this hook fires before EVERY Bash command and an unconditional ask nags on `ls`, which trains a human to click through the guard. And it NAMES THE PATH it tried, so the next occurrence diagnoses itself rather than needing a queue note. The path is passed through `tr` to forward slashes with quotes dropped before it is interpolated: a raw Windows backslash would make the document invalid JSON, and a discarded document turns this fail-closed layer into a silent fail-open.

hooks.command: command -v python >/dev/null 2>&1 && PY=python || PY=python3; H="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}/.claude/hooks/guard_ship.py"; "$PY" "$H" || { P=$(tr 'A-Z' 'a-z'); case "$P" in *git*|*"gh "*|*ssh*|*deploy.sh*|*mcp__github__*|*mcp__ccd_pr__*) J=$(printf '%s' "$H" | tr '\' '/' | tr -d '"'); printf '%s' '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"guard_ship.py could not run at all (no interpreter, file missing, or a syntax error). Asking rather than allowing, because the guard failed instead of confirming this call is safe. Tried: '"$J"'"},"systemMessage":"guard_ship.py could not run at '"$J"' -- asking rather than allowing."}' ;; esac; }
